finding: The round-level legacy fallback and the live clean predicate give opposite results for a round with an EMPTY surviving set. §4.1 makes a round clean when 'no surviving finding is of a blocking severity' — vacuously true when zero findings survive (a zero-finding round, or a round whose findings are all resolved wontfix/duplicate). But §3.4 says the fallback applies 'when no finding in the round carries a severity at all,' and for a new round recorded this release '--record computes that flag as not-clean.' A zero-finding round satisfies BOTH: no surviving blocking finding (→ clean per §4.1) and no per-finding severity present (→ not-clean per §3.4). Since a zero-finding round is historically the canonical clean/converging round, the literal §3.4 reading marks it not-clean and makes convergence unreachable. Two engineers write contradictory assertions; no test (5/6/7/19) pins the empty-surviving-set case.
suggestion: State that the round-level severity-less fallback applies only when the SURVIVING set is non-empty; an empty surviving set (zero findings, or all findings resolved wontfix/duplicate) is clean under the live predicate regardless of whether any finding carried severity. Add a test: a new round recorded this release with zero surviving findings is clean and counts toward convergence.

finding: §3.4 says a new round recorded this release whose findings carry no per-finding severity gets its clean flag computed as not-clean, justified as 'the all rule, since no severity can be shown non-blocking.' But a round with zero findings — reviewers returned nothing, the natural terminal state — also 'carries no per-finding severity at all' vacuously, yet the cited all rule ('no finding of any severity survives' = clean) makes an empty surviving set clean. The main clause (not-clean) and the parenthetical justification (the all rule) disagree for the empty-round case, so the clean flag of a genuinely empty new round is undefined; if computed not-clean, an actually-clean round is mis-marked and can never count toward convergence, and it also contradicts §4.2's premise that a clean round may have zero surviving findings.
suggestion: Scope the 'compute not-clean' rule to a round that has at least one finding but no severity on any of them. State explicitly that a round with zero (surviving) findings is clean under both blocking and all (the all rule applied to an empty set), independent of the severity-less legacy fallback.

finding: The round-6 sentence added to §3.4 — 'For such a new round recorded this release, --record computes that flag as not-clean (the all rule, since no severity can be shown non-blocking)' — is stated categorically over the set it just defined: 'A round whose recorded findings carry no per-finding severity.' By §4.1's own wording ('the round-level legacy fallback applies only when no finding in the round carries a severity at all') that set includes a round with ZERO findings, which is the canonical clean/terminal round. §3.4 routes any severity-less round to the persisted flag rather than the live recompute, so under this new sentence an empty-panel round is forced not-clean and can never count toward convergence — contradicting §3.2 ('clean when no surviving finding is of a blocking severity', trivially true for zero findings) and §3.3's all definition ('no finding of any severity survives', true for zero findings). The sentence is also internally inconsistent: the cited 'all rule' yields CLEAN for an empty surviving set, so 'the all rule' and 'not-clean' coincide only when at least one finding exists. Round 5 carried no such sentence, so this is introduced by the round-6 edit.
suggestion: Scope the 'computes that flag as not-clean' clause to a round that has at least one recorded finding all lacking severity (a non-empty severity-less panel); state explicitly that a round with zero findings stays clean because the all rule yields clean for an empty surviving set. Apply the same qualification to §11 test 5.

finding: The reconciliation story disagrees with itself about what the prior documentation promised. Overview table row 1 characterizes the documented rule as 'stop when no critical findings' (critical-only), and §3.1/§3.3 frame the release as making the tool 'do what its own documentation always promised' — implying the code is simply being aligned to an existing doc policy. But §4.1 states the new blocking set (critical+high) is the *union* of two mutually inconsistent sources — CLAUDE.md ('critical (blocking)', i.e. critical-only) and a prompt string ('critical/high') — and §9.2 instructs CLAUDE.md to be rewritten to 'critical or high block'. So the release actually widens the primary documented policy (critical-only) to critical+high; it does not merely enforce what the docs already said. A reader following the Overview would expect blocking=critical-only, then hit critical+high in §3.3/§4.1.
suggestion: Reword the Overview row and §3.1/§3.3 to say the docs were mutually inconsistent (critical-only vs critical/high) and this release reconciles them into critical+high — a deliberate widening of CLAUDE.md's line — rather than 'doing what the documentation always promised'. Keep the union framing of §4.1 as the single source of truth for what 'blocking' now means.

finding: §6.2 lets `tp audit <spec> --record <file> --harness-note "<text>"` store a note on an audit round, and §1 states the harness note 'extends to audit because [its] absence is symmetric,' but §6.3 specifies only `tp review --status` surfacing `harness_note`/`harness_stale`; no section says `tp audit --status` (or `--record`) emits them, and Test 11 does not disambiguate review vs audit. As written the audit-side harness note is write-only — storable but with no defined read path or staleness comparison — so an implementer cannot tell whether audit `--status` must emit these fields (nor whether §8.4's `--compact` stripping applies to the audit side).
suggestion: State explicitly that audit `--status`/`--record` surface `harness_note` and `harness_stale` symmetrically with review (and that `--compact` strips them there too), or, if intentionally review-only, remove the audit `--harness-note` storage from §6.2 so nothing is written without a read path.

finding: §6.3 has `--status` emit `harness_note` — the latest round's full verbatim free text — on every non-compact call, regardless of `harness_stale`. §8.4 concedes the note 'can run long', and the only decision signal derived from the wrapper is the `harness_stale` boolean that tp computes internally (§6.3); the note body feeds no agent decision and is stripped entirely under `--compact` (§8.4). On a non-drift round (harness_stale=false) the long note text is echoed with nothing actionable in it — output bytes the agent parses without a decision behind them.
suggestion: Emit `harness_note` only when `harness_stale` is true (drift detected), where an operator needs to see WHAT the framing changed to; when notes agree or there is no drift, the `harness_stale=false` boolean alone carries the signal. This keeps the recorded note in `.tp-review/` for audit while removing the always-on long-text echo from the `--status` response.

finding: §6.3/Test 11 pin harness_note as 'the latest round's note' but never specify its JSON representation when the latest recorded round carries no note (predate or opt-out per §6.2): absent key, null, or empty string. §8.4 uses 'omitted' for the compact case, hinting at absence, but the non-compact no-note case is unstated. Two engineers write different assertions (field missing vs. "" vs. null) for a --status against a round with no --harness-note.
suggestion: State the representation explicitly, e.g. 'when the latest round carries no note, harness_note is omitted from the response (never emitted as an empty string or null)', and cover it in Test 11.

finding: §8.4 specifies that --compact omits harness_note and harness_stale (retaining next_action and nonblocking_open) only for 'tp review --status' and '--record'. But §6.2 extends --harness-note to the audit loop and §6.3 defines harness_note/harness_stale on --status without distinguishing review from audit, so audit --status presumably also emits them. The spec never states whether 'tp audit --status/--record --compact' strips harness_note/harness_stale, leaving review and audit compaction asymmetric. Test 18 tests only 'tp review --status --compact', so the audit compaction behavior is both unspecified and untested.
suggestion: State in §8.4 that the same --compact stripping (harness_note/harness_stale omitted, next_action retained) applies to the audit --status/--record equivalents, and extend Test 18 to assert 'tp audit --status --compact' behavior — or explicitly note if audit --compact intentionally differs.
